reason: Reproduced by driving master.html?v=approach&state=day at 390x844 and opening .b-behindSummary. The numbers are exact: ticks at y 640/668/682/696/724/738/948/1160, copy centres at 650/699/748/797/846/895/958/1170; drift per row 10, 31, 66, 101, 122, 157, 10, 10 px, identical at 390/768/1152/1440 because the morning renders in a fixed device frame. The cause is in place() (render-b.js): top = away*px pins the tick and the count to the true pixel while only .b-copy takes --push, and at BACK_PX=2 six of eight rows go data-crowded="true". .b-away is absolutely positioned at top:2px so the COUNT stays with the tick, not the row - which is worse than the finding says. On the rendered screen 'Final guest numbers' (28 back) has 28, 35 and 42 stacked against it and 'Choose the evening music' (35 back) has 56 and 63 against it, so the readout is not merely absent from three rows, it is beside the wrong row on two. On the forward measure the same mechanism is clean - every guest row measures exactly 10px tick-to-copy, nothing crowded - so this is specific to .b-back, not a complaint about the instrument. Not gate-covered and not a restatement: collisions() in interaction-check.mjs deliberately measures only .b-copy against .b-copy ('the tick and the count sit on the true pixel; the words are what must not overlap'), and the back-rail block asserts only px===2, exact top placement, the heading, and no accent. Nothing anywhere asserts that a mark or a count stays with the row it names. No constraint is touched: a hairline at a tint of Ink adds no hue and no weight, and the architecture is greenfield. Two corrections to the finding's own text, neither of which saves it: the 948/846 example is mis-stated (nothing is at 846, so no reader lands on a neighbour's mark there - the real collisions are the two named above), and print does not use this rail at all (states.print calls behindBlock({print:true}), which renders the .b-behindRows table), so 'same treatment in the print variant' is void.
sharpenedFix: Do not draw the proposed L in the rail-to-copy gutter: that gutter measures 20px at every width, so a vertical leader up to 157px tall sitting 8px off the rail would read as a second rail on a 390 phone, and .b-item[data-crowded="true"] .b-copy already knocks out a 12px halo across it. Fix the louder half first and the geometry gets easy: the count is a readout of the row, not a mark on the rail, so give .b-item the --push (place() already computes it) and set .b-away { top: calc(2px + var(--push)) } so every number travels with its own title - that alone kills 28/35/42 sitting against 'Final guest numbers' and restores a number to the three rows that have none. Then connect only the mark: for data-crowded="true", a 1px hairline at var(--fore-24) from the tick centre left across the 14px lane to the count column's right edge, then down to the count's centre, then a short stub - the lane between .b-away (ends x 96) and the rail (x 110) is empty and is the only place on this screen a leader can run without competing with the rail. Hang it off the shared .b-item[data-crowded="true"] rule rather than a .b-back-only patch, so the same law answers crowding in both directions; the forward measure never crowds today, so nothing there changes.
